name: Saint Januarius
history: Bishop of Benevento, martyred near Naples in the persecution of Diocletian around 305, and venerated as the patron of that city. A phial said to hold his blood is kept in Naples cathedral; on his feast and on other days each year the dried mass has repeatedly been seen to liquefy. The Church permits the devotion without pronouncing on its cause.
life: Little is certain about Januarius beyond his martyrdom, and the accounts of his death were written long afterwards. Tradition holds that he went to visit Christians imprisoned at Pozzuoli, was arrested himself, was thrown to wild beasts that would not touch him, and was beheaded near the Solfatara with several companions. His relics were moved more than once over the centuries and came back to Naples for good in 1497. The liquefaction of the blood was first recorded in 1389 and has been observed many times since, usually on the Saturday before the first Sunday of May, on 19 September and on 16 December, before crowds who pray for it. Neapolitans credit him with protecting their city, especially during the eruption of Vesuvius in 1631. Scientists have proposed explanations, and the Church has made no formal judgement: the devotion rests on faith and prayer, not on dogma.
prayerTo: Saint Januarius, bishop and martyr, you gave your life for Christ, and your people have trusted in your prayers for centuries. Pray for the city of Naples and for all who live in the shadow of danger, and for me, that my faith may not be dry and hard but warm and living. Amen.
penance: Pray today for Christians who face death for their faith, and give alms in their name to a charity that supports the persecuted Church.
meditation: Each year the people of Naples wait and pray for the blood to liquefy. Is there a hardened place in your heart that you could ask God to soften?
